items.title: Bitcoin's rally above $72K is a fakeout, not a breakout. The Treasury buyback announcement caught markets by surprise. Bitcoin investors have long believed a return to easy money would be the catalyst for gold and Bitcoin to soar. They are only half right. Sell Bitcoin, buy gold.

items.title: The U.S. national debt is over $40 trillion, with $11.58 trillion added on Trump's watch, the most of any president. Obama is in second place with $9.32 trillion, but Trump has almost 2.5 years left to add to his lead. Biden still holds the single-term record with $8.47 trillion.

items.title: Treasury's policy choice of trading higher inflation to slow the rise of long-term interest rates has not only pushed up precious metals, but Bitcoin too. The big difference is that gold and silver will not only hold today's gains, but add to them. In contrast, Bitcoin is a sell.

items.title: On our national debt, the average coupon on maturities beyond ten years is 3.44%. That's way below current long-term rates. Buying that debt back now is like a homeowner refinancing a 3.44% 30-year fixed-rate mortgage into a 4% one-year ARM. Who would be dumb enough to do that?

items.title: Bond yields may be down today, but oil is up 1.5%, above $86. That's because Treasury traded lower yields for a weaker dollar, which pushes up oil and other commodity prices. That means more economic pressure on the Fed to hike rates, but more political pressure to cut them.

items.title: Markets like inflation, but the general public won't. The Dow is up 330 points, about 0.6%. But gold is up $160, which is 3.7%. So nominal asset prices rise, but real values fall. Consumer prices will rise too, offsetting the benefits of higher asset prices for most Americans.

items.title: In a rising interest rate environment the smart move is to issue long-term debt, locking in lower rates. But Treasury can't do that, as increased issuance of longer-maturity debt would crash the economy now. So instead they'll crash the economy later when short-term debt matures.
items.content:

— Peter Schiff (@PeterSchiff) Aug 19, 2026

items.title: As the Treasury issues short-term debt to buy back previously issued long-term debt, its interest expense goes up, as the coupons on the debt it buys back are lower than the rates it pays on the money it borrows. The national debt rises faster while the average maturity falls.

items.title: Treasury just announced that it will buy more long-term Treasuries private investors no longer want to hold to try to keep yields from rising. The money to pay for it will ultimately be created by the Fed, sending inflation soaring. That's why gold is already up $125 on the news!

items.title: Today some investors are likely rotating a bit from equities to bonds. This trade is bound to pick up as bond prices continue to fall and yields rise. I don't think yields will rise high enough to make bonds a good investment, but in the short run they may lose less than stocks.

items.title: Traders selling gold today still don't understand what's happening. Rising bond yields won't compete with gold, they'll drive more money into gold. As inflation causes bonds to lose value, investors seeking to avoid losses will sell and buy gold as an alternative store of value.
